title: On the world stage, Xi projects confidence
gist: Isabel Hilton argues that Xi Jinping's courteous, Global South-focused diplomacy, delivered through Brics, the SCO, the New Development Bank, de-dollarisation initiatives and a new open-source AI offer, is successfully positioning China against an embattled Trump. China's rare-earth leverage and Trump's Iran war give Xi the upper hand, including on Taiwan.

insights.claim: Xi's phrase 'changes unseen in one hundred years', borrowed from political scientist Yuan Peng, is shorthand for the eastward shift of economic power and relative US decline, and has anchored his global diplomacy since 2017.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Beijing's strategy assumes structural US decline; expect patient, long-horizon positioning.
insights.quote: changes unseen in one hundred years

insights.claim: China presents itself as a courteous, reliable partner sharing trade and technology gains, in contrast with a violent, declining superpower whose president humiliates visiting leaders, and Hilton says this approach is yielding benefits.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: China's diplomatic soft power is gaining at US expense; relevant to Global South trade and FDI flows.
insights.locator: That diplomacy has been highly visible

insights.claim: Xi made his first visit to India in seven years for the 18th Brics summit in Delhi, shortly after the SCO gathering in Bishkek on 31 August, and Brics now represents 40 per cent of the global economy.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: The growing weight of non-Western blocs in global GDP; watch China-India thaw.
insights.quote: Brics now represents 40 per cent of the global economy
insights.locator: That diplomacy has been highly visible

insights.claim: Brics lacks strategic alignment: the UAE, which hosts US bases and was attacked by Iran, halted all trade and financial transactions with Iran on 19 August, and the summit issued only a bland call for Middle East peace after May's foreign ministers failed to agree a statement.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Don't expect Brics to act as a bloc on security; UAE-Iran trade halt is a Gulf trade and finance datapoint.
insights.locator: These organisations have no binding collective

insights.claim: Despite lacking alignment, Brics is not meaningless: it is one of several institutions China uses to claim leadership of the 'majority world' through a narrative of rebalancing after Western exploitation of the Global South.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Discount the 'Brics is irrelevant' consensus; its institutional plumbing matters.
insights.locator: The lack of strategic alignment in the Brics

insights.claim: The Brics New Development Bank, launched in 2014, has approved billions of dollars of infrastructure and development projects in Global South countries China argues were neglected by existing multilateral banks.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Alternative development finance is eroding World Bank-style incumbency; a signal for EM infrastructure lending.
insights.locator: The claim is bolstered with practical measures

insights.claim: Brics is promoting easier cross-border payments, resilient supply chains, more trade in national currencies and IMF reform to reduce the influence of the US dollar.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Gradual de-dollarisation of trade flows; watch local-currency settlement volumes and payment rails.
insights.locator: In the same spirit, Brics has promoted

insights.claim: Xi told the Brics summit China will initiate a Brics open-source AI ecosystem, disseminating Chinese AI models at low or no cost and supporting cooperation on large language models, seminars and training.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Chinese open-weight models could become default infrastructure across the Global South, a competitive threat to US AI vendors' international growth.
insights.quote: disseminating Chinese AI models at low or no cost
insights.locator: In the same spirit, Brics has promoted

insights.claim: China is widely considered a close competitor with the US on AI.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: The AI race is near parity in perception; relevant to US tech valuations and export-control policy.
insights.locator: Since the start of Trump’s second term

insights.claim: Since Trump's second term began, China has weathered the worst of the tariffs and forced the US to a standstill through its control of rare earths and strategic mineral supplies.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Rare-earth and critical-mineral chokepoints are China's decisive trade weapon; supports non-China critical-minerals supply plays.
insights.locator: Since the start of Trump’s second term

insights.claim: China reportedly threatened to cancel the 24 September Washington summit if the US approved new Taiwan arms sales, after the US paused $14bn of planned sales in May citing the demands of its war with Iran.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: US Taiwan support is being traded off; watch defence-contractor Taiwan orders and cross-strait risk.
insights.locator: It is a clear sign of Chinese confidence

insights.claim: Hilton suggests Xi may reasonably judge that a US president bogged down in a pointless war and sinking in the polls needs the summit more than he does, letting China play hardball on Taiwan, though this does not signal readiness for a military assault.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Expect Chinese negotiating leverage at the Xi-Trump summits (Washington, G20 in Miami), not invasion risk.
insights.locator: Xi could be justified in thinking

insights.claim: Xi has visited more than 70 countries since 2012, building Global South influence in Africa and Latin America through events such as FOCAC summits with 50+ African leaders, while Trump has never visited Africa and visited Latin America only once as president.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Long-run Chinese influence in commodity-rich regions; US playing catch-up via Rubio.
insights.locator: Xi has been building influence in the Global South
